tempo.basis: from three complete recordings, median 2:30 (Phoenix Classics, 36 arie di stile antico 2:30, Haman 2:28, Cafiero/Di Luccia 2:35), 1.5 s allowed for silence; Donaudy marks it Allegro mosso (counting the D.S. al Fine: bars 8–50 sung twice)

phrases: Blow, then, blow around my beloved,
spiˈraːte pur spiˈraːte atˈtorno‿a lo ˈmiːo ˈbɛːne
little breezes, and make sure whether she holds me in her heart,

whether she holds me in her heart.
If she holds me in her heart,

if she holds me in her heart,
se nel ˈsuːo kɔr mi ˈtjɛːne

vatʧerˈtaːte ˈaure beˈaːte ˈaure ˈljɛːvi‿e beˈaːte

notes: Words by Alberto Donaudy; No. 10 of Stefano Donaudy's 36 Arie di stile antico (published 1918). The song ends with D.S. al Fine: the last phrase "Spi-" is the pickup back to the sign at bar 8, and the song ends at Fine in bar 50. IPA follows sung Italian: open and closed e and o marked, double consonants written double, stress marked on words of two or more syllables; words joined by ‿ share a note. Literal translation, for meaning.
